target_customer: Space companies, space agencies and in-space data center builders needing lunar-made materials
problem: Terawatt scale data centers and other space infrastructure are limited by the cost of launching solar panel materials from Earth.
business_model: Lunar resource processing and construction services, customer commitments reported as letters of intent

founders.name: Ross Centers
founders.background_notes: Lunar resource geologist per the YC page.

founders.name: Brogan BamBrogan
founders.background_notes: YC page lists CTO; Payload in 2024 listed him as VP of customer operations and integration.

competitors.name: Blue Origin (Blue Alchemist)
competitors.what: Molten regolith electrolysis to make silicon solar cells and cover glass
competitors.traction_then: Reported silicon above 99.999 percent purity on simulant

competitors.name: Maana Electric
competitors.what: Molten salt electrolysis to make silicon solar cells from low-value feedstock for ISRU

technical_complexity.rationale: Melting and electrolyzing regolith in hard vacuum and producing solar-grade silicon on the Moon is research-grade and needs lunar delivery.

defensibility.rationale: Process know-how and SpaceX-derived team are hard to copy, but Blue Origin has a larger NASA-funded effort.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Blue Origin was already funded for the same wedge.

market_need_then: Demand for in-space compute and power is speculative; the YC page claims 1B dollars in letters of intent, which are non-binding.

identity.voice_and_tone: Ambitious infrastructure framing: 'Infrastructure for Terawatt Scaling'.

branding.community_and_virality: Founder interviewed on the Space Strategy podcast (2025); Payload covered the stealth emergence in June 2024.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic real-word name, but space press has covered the company; no source states a brand effect.

pivots.from: Lunar landing pads and propellant infrastructure
pivots.to: Silicon for solar panels powering in-space data centers
pivots.why: Not stated; inferred from differing descriptions in 2024 press and the 2026 YC page, so treated as a shift in emphasis.

outcome_analysis: Ethos is a long-gestating lunar startup that emerged from stealth in 2024 with SpaceX alumni and entered YC in Summer 2026 with a data center framing. No outcome yet. Success hinges on proving the process on a lunar mission and funding it against Blue Origin, so technical risk dominates.
notes: Payload (June 2024) named Jeff Overbeek as COO and 14 employees; YC lists two founders and team size 2. YC page cites a completed NASA contract but Payload says a partner, Astrolab, holds the NASA award. Aggregators list a 125K YC seed (Dealroom), an Aug 2024 seed and a 2025 grant (CB Insights, Caplight); all unverified, no round recorded. The pivot entry is an interpretation of differing descriptions.
